title: CE-antiferromagnetic electronic structure in LaSr$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ revealed by micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and tight-binding models
authors: Yasutaka Sawata, Yudai Hirai, Rintaro Miyabayashi, Goro Shibata, Hideki Kuwahara, Miho Kitamura, Koji Horiba, Kenichi Ozawa, Noriaki Hamada, Tomohiko Saitoh
abstract: We have investigated the electronic structure of LaSr$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ in the CE-type antiferromagnetic (CE-AFM) state below the Néel temperature using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy ($μ$-ARPES) and tight-binding models. In agreement with the tight-binding calculations, we found a dispersive intensity around the X point in the $μ$-ARPES spectra, where the A-type antiferromagnetic (A-AFM) phase has no bands experimentally and theoretically, demonstrating that we have successfully captured the signatures of the CE-AFM band structure for the first time. Many observed features can be explained by the CE-AFM tight-binding bands, although some of them and the overall near-Fermi level intensity mapping can be explained by the A-AFM band structure. This indicates that the CE-AFM domain size would be no larger than the beam footprint size of a $\sim\!20$~{\textmu}m scale.
summary: This work investigates the electronic structure of LaSr2Mn2O7 in its CE-antiferromagnetic state by combining $\mu$-ARPES experiments with tight-binding theory. The authors successfully demonstrate that the observed band dispersions are best explained by a model incorporating the CE-AFM magnetic ordering, distinguishing it from simpler A-AFM structures. This provides crucial experimental evidence for understanding charge and orbital ordering in these complex manganites.
main_problem: The study aims to experimentally and theoretically reveal the electronic structure of LaSr2Mn2O7 when it is in its CE-type antiferromagnetic (CE-AFM) state.
main_result: The $\mu$-ARPES measurements revealed a dispersive intensity around the X point, which was successfully explained by the CE-AFM tight-binding model for the first time. This confirms the electronic signature of the CE-AFM phase in this material.
method: The research combines experimental micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy ($\mu$-ARPES) with theoretical analysis using detailed tight-binding models derived from LDA+U calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is LaSr2Mn2O7, focusing on the CE-AFM state characterized by charge and orbital ordering. Theoretical modeling involves single-layered (2D) tight-binding Hamiltonians incorporating both FM and AF hopping integrals to capture the complex magnetic structure.
key_observables: Electronic band dispersion relations measured via $\mu$-ARPES intensity plots, particularly at high-symmetry points like X and M in the folded Brillouin Zone ($\Gamma_{	ext{CE}}$).
important_parameters: The analysis compares CE-AFM vs. A-AFM states; key energy scales include hopping integrals (e.g., $	ilde{t}_{dd\sigma} = -0.652 	ext{ eV}$) and the magnetic ordering type.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that the observed features are governed by the CE-AFM band structure, although some near-Fermi level intensity mapping might suggest A-AFM contributions; the domain size is estimated to be $\lesssim 20 \mu	ext{m}$.
figures_summary: Figures compare ARPES data (intensity and second derivative) along specific high-symmetry directions ($\Gamma-	ext{V}/	ext{UCE}-\Gamma	ext{CE}$), showing that the CE-AFM model successfully reproduces band features at both $\Gamma_{	ext{CE}}$ points, unlike the A-AFM structure.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the scientific problem by comparing different magnetic states (CE-AFM vs. A-AFM). It details the theoretical framework using tight-binding models and presents experimental $\mu$-ARPES results that are then used to validate the CE-AFM model over the A-AFM model, concluding with a discussion of domain size.
why_interesting: The detailed comparison between different magnetic ordering states (CE-AFM vs. A-AFM) using spectroscopic techniques provides deep insight into how electronic structure is intrinsically linked to complex magnetic ground states in strongly correlated oxides.
